source_text:
Πάλιν μοι λέγει: Ἀλήθειαν ἀγάπα καὶ πᾶσα ἀλήθεια ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου ἐκπορευέσθω, ἵνα τὸ πνεῦμα. ὃ ὁ θεὸς κατῴκισεν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ ταύτῃ, ἀληθὲς εὑρεθῇ παρὰ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις, καὶ οὕτως δοξασθήσεται ὁ κύριος ὁ ἐν σοὶ κατοικῶν, ὅτι ὁ κύριος ἀληθινὸς ἐν παντὶ ῥήματι καὶ οὐδὲν παῤ αὐτῷ ψεῦδος.
οἱ οὖν ψευδόμενοι ἀθετοῦσι τὸν κύριον καὶ γίνονται ἀποστερηταὶ στερηταὶ τοῦ κυρίου, μὴ παραδιδόντες αὐτῷ τὴν παρακαταθήκην, ἣν ἔλαβον. ἔλαβον γὰρ παῤ αὐτοῦ πνεῦμα ἄψευστον. τοῦτο ἐὰν ψευδὲς ἀποδώσωσιν, ἐμίαναν τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀποστερηταί.
ταῦτα οὖν ἀκούσας ἐγὼ ἔκλαυσα λίαν. ἰδὼν δέ με κλαίοντα λέγει: Τί κλαίεις; Ὅτι, φημί, κύριε, οὐκ οἶδα, εἰ δύναμαι σωθῆναι. Διατί; φησίν. Οὐδέπω γάρ, φημί, κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἐμῇ ζωῇ ἀληθὲς ἐλάλησα ῥῆμα, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε πανούργως ἐλάλησα μετὰ πάντων καὶ τὸ ψεῦδός μου ἀληθὲς ἐπέδειξα παρὰ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις: καὶ οὐδέποτέ μοι οὐδεὶς ἀντεῖπεν, ἀλλ’ ἐπιστεύθη τῷ λόγῳ μου. πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, δύναμαι ζῆσαι ταῦτα πράξας;
Σὺ μέν, φησί, καλῶς καὶ ἀληθῶς φρονεῖς: ἔδει γάρ σε ὡς θεοῦ δοῦλον ἐν ἀληθείᾳ πορεύεσθαι, καὶ πονηρὰν συνείδησιν μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ἀληθείας μὴ κατοικεῖν μηδὲ λύπην ἐπάγειν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ σεμνῷ καὶ ἀληθεῖ. Οὐδέποτε, φημί, κύριε, τοιαῦτα ῥήματα ἀκριβῶς ἤκουσα.
Νῦν οὖν, φησίν, ἀκούεις: φύλασσε αὐτά, ἵνα καὶ τὰ πρότερον ἃ ἐλάλησας ψευδὴ ἐν ταῖς πραγματείαις σου, τούτων εὑρεθέντων ἀληθινῶν, κἀκεῖνα πιστὰ γένηται: δύναται γὰρ κἀκεῖνα πιστὰ γενέσθαι. ἐὰν ταῦτα φυλάξῃς καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πᾶσαν ἀλήθειαν λαλήσῃς, δυνήσῃ σεαυτῷ ζωὴν περιποιήσασθαι: καὶ ὃς ἂν ἀκούσῃ τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην καὶ ἀπέξεται τοῦ πονηροτάτου ψεύσματος ζήσεται τῷ θεῷ.
thought_title: Love truth and speak no lie
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the third commandment: love truth and tell no lies. Hermas weeps, because he has lied all his life in business.
pass_a_gloss: Again he says to me: Love truth and let all truth go out from your mouth, so that the spirit, which God settled in this flesh, may be found true among all people, and so the Lord who dwells in you will be glorified, because the Lord is true in every word and there is no lie with him. So those who lie reject the Lord and become defrauders of the Lord, not handing over to him the deposit which they received. For they received from him a spirit without lie. If they give this back false, they defiled the commandment of the Lord and became defrauders. So when I heard these things I wept greatly. And seeing me weeping he says: Why do you weep? Because, I say, Lord, I do not know if I can be saved. Why? he says. For not yet, I say, Lord, in my life have I spoken a true word, but always I spoke craftily with everyone and I showed my lie as true among all people: and never did anyone contradict me, but my word was believed. How then, I say, Lord, can I live, having done these things? You, he says, think well and truly: for it was necessary for you, as a servant of God, to walk in truth, and not to let an evil conscience dwell with the spirit of truth, nor to bring grief to the spirit that is reverent and true. Never, I say, Lord, have I heard such words accurately. Now then, he says, you hear: keep them, so that also the former things which you spoke falsely in your business dealings, when these are found true, those also may become trustworthy: for those also can become trustworthy. If you keep these things and from now on speak all truth, you will be able to secure life for yourself: and whoever hears this commandment and abstains from the most evil lie will live to God.

choices.why: The term means those who withhold or rob what belongs to another; 'defrauders' captures the legal-economic force of withholding the deposit from the Lord.
A technical term for something entrusted for safekeeping; 'deposit' preserves the banking metaphor of the spirit entrusted by God.
The adverb describes cunning, deceptive speech; 'craftily' conveys the deliberate slyness without modernizing to 'deceitfully'.
The noun refers to commercial transactions; 'business dealings' makes clear the context of Hermas's former life as a businessman.
The adjective describes the Spirit as worthy of awe and honor; 'reverent' fits the Spirit's character rather than 'holy' which would be a different Greek word.
The dative expresses the one to whom the life is lived; 'live to God' preserves the dative force and the theological idiom of living for God.

pass_b_english: Again the Shepherd said to me, “Love truth, and let everything that comes from your mouth be truth, so that the spirit God has made to dwell in this flesh may be found true by all people. In this way the Lord who dwells in you will be glorified. For the Lord is true in every word, and with him there is no lie.

“So those who lie reject the Lord. They become defrauders of the Lord, for they do not give back to him the deposit they received. They received from him a spirit that does not lie. If they give it back a lying spirit, they have defiled the Lord’s commandment and become defrauders.”
When I heard this, I wept bitterly. Seeing me weep, he said, “Why are you weeping?”
“Because, sir,” I said, “I do not know whether I can be saved.”

“Because, sir,” I said, “never yet in my life have I spoken a true word. I have always spoken craftily with everyone, and I passed my lie off as truth before all people. No one ever contradicted me. My word was believed. How then, sir,” I said, “can I live, after doing these things?”

“Your thinking is right and true,” he said. “For as God’s servant you ought to have walked in truth. An evil conscience ought not to have dwelt with the spirit of truth, and you ought not to have brought grief upon the spirit that is revered and true.”
“Never, sir,” I said, “have I heard such words so exactly.”

“Well, now you hear them,” he said. “Keep them, so that even the lies you told before in your business dealings may become trustworthy, once these words are found true. For those too can become trustworthy. If you keep these things, and from now on speak nothing but truth, you will be able to gain life for yourself. And whoever hears this commandment and keeps away from lying, that most wicked thing, will live to God.”

checks.via: blind check of the tuned English, clean at round 0 (tune_check.py)

polish.changed: Broke the long dialogue into separate paragraphs for each speaker turn, clarified that Hermas is the one weeping and speaking, and made the Shepherd's responses distinct so the exchange reads naturally aloud.

notes.quote: When I heard these things, I wept bitterly
notes.why: Hermas speaks without clear transition from Shepherd's words

polish.changed: Clarified that the Shepherd is the one speaking to Hermas after the quotation, and smoothed the dialogue transitions so the speaker is always clear.

notes.quote: When I heard these things, I wept bitterly. Seeing me weeping, he says: "Why are you weeping?"
notes.why: The 'he' is unclear after the quotation marks; could be God, Shepherd, or another figure.
Unusual term; likely means 'embezzlers' or 'faithless stewards' of God's deposit (truth).
notes.fix: Use 'faithless stewards' or add note explaining 'defrauders' as embezzlers of divine trust.

polish.changed: Re-tuned from the Greek for listening: speaker tags, sentence rhythm, plain modern diction; mistranslations fixed (outputs/viapatrum/hermas-tune-20261117/final).

last_rejected.why: "Without lie" is unidiomatic and obscures meaning; ἄψευστον means "truthful, true, not false" (active sense), not merely "without lie" (passive absence).
last_rejected.ruling: ἄψευστον means 'without lie/falsehood'; 'without lie' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ψευδὲς here is adverbial/qualitative "as false, falsely," not "as a lying spirit" which personifies and changes meaning.
last_rejected.ruling: ψευδὲς modifies πνεῦμα implied; 'lying spirit' fits context of returning the spirit falsely.

last_rejected.why: ἀκριβῶς here means "carefully, exactly, in detail" (i.e., he never heard such teachings before), not "with precision" which suggests rhetorical exactness.
last_rejected.fix: heard such words so exactly before
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκριβῶς means 'exactly, precisely'; 'with precision' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: πραγματείαις means "transactions, affairs, dealings" broadly, not specifically "business dealings"; this over-specifies and may mislead about Hermas's occupation.
last_rejected.ruling: πραγματείαις means 'affairs, business, transactions'; 'business dealings' is within range.

last_rejected.why: ζήσεται τῷ θεῷ is a Semitic/LXX idiom meaning "live for God, live in God's service, live unto God" (dative of advantage/reference), not merely "to God" which is ambiguous.
last_rejected.ruling: ζήσεται τῷ θεῷ with dative; 'live to God' is standard rendering of this LXX idiom.
